title: AI music streaming fraud earns first prison sentence
key_facts: Michael Smith, 54, was sentenced to 18 months in prison plus two years of supervised release on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 in Manhattan federal court.
He pleaded guilty in March to wire fraud conspiracy for generating thousands of AI songs and streaming them billions of times with bots.
The scheme brought in more than $8 million in royalties, which he agreed to forfeit.
It is described as the first criminal conviction over streaming fraud.
Prosecutors had asked for at least 46 months; probation recommended 24; his lawyers said the harm to any one artist was "insignificant".
quote_evidence: A man who used AI songs to steal millions in music royalties has been sentenced to 18 months in prison, capping off the first-ever criminal case over streaming fraud.
Judge John G. Koeltl ordered him to serve a year and a half in jail, followed by two years of supervised release.
why_it_matters_hint: First prison term for AI-assisted streaming fraud sets a precedent, though shorter than prosecutors sought.
